 Early voting underway in West Virginia
 By 
 Lori Kersey 
 - 
 October 21, 2026 6:00 am 
 Early voting starts today in West Virginia. An early voting sign is shown on May 8, 2026 in Charleston, West Virginia. (Photo by Leann Ray/West Virginia Watch)
 West Virginia voters can now vote in the 2026 general election at courthouses and community locations across the state. 
 Early voting started Tuesday, Oct. 21 and will continue on through the end of the month, including Saturday Oct. 24 and Oct. 31. A complete list of early voting locations is available on the Secretary of State’s website, govotewv.com . 
 2026 Voter Guide
 The candidates, the ballot measures, and the tools you need to cast your vote.
 Check it out 
 This is the first statewide general election that voters will be required to show photo identification under a new law. According to the Secretary of State’s Office, the following forms of identification are acceptable:
 Drivers license or state-issued ID
 U.S. passport or passport card
 Employee ID with photo issued by a state, local or federal government
 Student ID from West Virginia school
 U.S. military ID with photo
 Voter registration card with photo issued by country clerk or Secretary of State’s Office
 An ID issued by the DMV without a photo for voters who attest that they’re part of a recognized religious community that prohibits them from being photographed
 West Virginia voters will choose representatives for two seats in the U.S. House of Representatives and one in the U.S. Senate, as well as a host of seats in the West Virginia Senate and House of Delegates. 
 Voters will decide on a constitutional amendment. If more than 50% of voters approve Amendment 1, the state’s constitution would be amended to include that “Only citizens of the United States who are citizens of this state shall be entitled to vote at all elections.”  
 Certification write-in candidates are seeking election to one statewide federal office, seven for legislative offices, and to several local offices, according to the Secretary of State’s Office.  
 Sample ballots for each of the state’s 55 counties are also available at the Secretary of State’s website .  
 The general election is Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026.
